title: Magimagi sennit cord
summary: Magimagi is cord plaited from coconut-husk fibre, flat in rows of chevrons, then lashed to frames and mats. Black, red-brown and cream cords draw the bands. Copy the pattern, which mirrors both ways.
howToPlay: Pick a cord colour and a pattern shape.
Plait it in; the mirrored places are plaited too.
Check the cordwork against the pattern.
Watch and learn shows a finished round, one placement at a time.
rules: The cordwork mirrors left to right and top to bottom.
Placing the same shape in the same colour again, or choosing the eraser, clears it and its mirror partners.
The result compares your piece with the pattern cell by cell: three stars at 98 percent or more, two at 85, one at 60.
The pattern to copy is always shown beside the work and as a faint guide on the cloth.
heritageNote: Magimagi is the coconut-fibre cord of Fiji, plaited by hand and used to lash house frames, canoes and mats. Its black and red-brown chevron bands are a familiar sight in Fijian building.
credits: Pattern designs are original arrangements in the tradition's motif vocabulary.
